The page is about the ALLPOWERS R4000 power station alone. It doesn't recommend a solar panel, so it doesn't deliver the "combo" in your title.

**Price**
- The store price is $1,499, against a "list" price of $3,299.
- Code **EXTRA12** takes $179.88 off, which brings it to **$1,319.12**. It's 12% off orders over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. The site says it tested the code in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23.
- The other two codes save less. ALLPOWERS26 and EXTRA10 each take off $149.90, for $1,349.10.
- The checkout usually takes one code per order, so use EXTRA12.
- Buy here: [ALLPOWERS R4000 at ALLPOWERS's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). It's an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Specs that matter for an RV**
- **Capacity:** 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, rated for 3,500+ cycles.
- **AC output:** 3,600 W continuous on US 120 V, with a 6,000 W peak. The "4,000 W" in the name is the 230 V rating, so it overstates what you get in the US.
- **RV outlet:** It has an RV outlet plus 4 standard outlets.
- **Solar input:** Up to 2,000 W across 3 inputs, at 650 W each and 12–60 V. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W. A single input maxes out at 650 W.
- **AC recharge:** About 2 hours from a wall outlet at 2,000 W.
- **Weight:** 45 kg (about 99 lb), so you won't be hand-carrying it much.
- **Warranty:** 5 years.

**Caveats**
- The site's own "who it's for" is whole-circuit home backup or job sites. For an RV, the weight and size mean you'd likely mount it in one spot.
- The 30-day return window covers unused items only, and you pay return shipping unless the unit is defective. ALLPOWERS's refund page also says sale items can't be returned, and this unit is on sale. Check that before you buy.
- The page doesn't say which panels pair well with it. Match the panel voltage to the 12–60 V input range.

I can look for panels that suit the R4000, such as 400 W rigid or portable ones, if you'd like. If you tell me your RV's daily power use, I can also check whether 3.5 kWh is the right size.
